title: When Counterfactual Queries Are Well Defined across Micro-Level Realizations of Causal Abstractions
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field; calibrated salvageable=false; paper_score_ceiling 5.6 < 7.4, and the only field route is a substantial new selector-width research program.
gap_reasons: The note proves an exact but worst-case exhaustive affine-hull test, a sufficient backward-congruence test, an XP bounded-interaction test in a one-root regime, and a coNP-hardness result obtained by embedding CNF constancy.

It does not deliver an exact non-enumerative structural characterization for general parent-routed reusable sections, and the proposed selector-aware width framework is explicitly left open and unseparated from standard factor-graph dynamic programming.

The elementary nature of the affine recursion and hardness reduction, unresolved comparison to generic algorithms, and absence of a broader causal or econometric consequence constrain the projected leading-journal score.
proof_attempt_summary: The run built a fixed-law reusable-section decision theory using an exhaustive affine-hull certificate, explicit rational separating sections, a one-root XP interaction test, and a CNF constancy hardness reduction. D0.5 found that these results remain incremental because the useful general certificate is exhaustive and the non-enumerative structural test is only sufficient; three local soundness defects also remain unrepaired. Reaching the field floor would require a new exact selector-width FPT canonicality-and-witness algorithm plus a representation-stable separation from augmented-factor-graph dynamic programming.
tldr: Given explicit worlds \(w\mapsto(I_w,a_w)\), the project asks exactly when a finite L2/L3 polynomial query has one value under every parent-compatible deterministic right inverse, with each routed selector choice reused across all of its occurrences. It proposes an exact recursive affine certificate or two rationally separated sections, a response-table backward-congruence certificate that is near-linear in the relevant explicit tables, an explicit linear-size family on which that certificate validates \(2^n\) sections although full AIC fails and fixed-query graph pruning removes nothing, a \(dk\) interaction test for one root treatment, and a succinct coNP-complete boundary. Representative invariance, causal partitions, model-level abstraction, and counterfactual-graph pruning are treated as comparators rather than renamed contributions.
gap: Query-specific AIC already states representative equality, fundamental causal partitions already group micro-treatments with equal outcome laws, model-level abstraction criteria already enforce intervention commutation, and counterfactual graphs already prune fixed queries. What is not supplied by those results is an exact fixed-law test for explicit multiworld queries under globally reusable parent-routed sections, together with a local response-table quotient whose gain survives ordinary ancestor pruning.
fill: Establish the exact one-way comparator implications, prove the backward-congruence theorem and its linear-size exponential-separation family, retain the exact affine certificate and rational failure pair, prove the root-treatment \(dk\) test and succinct coNP boundary, and leave selector width open absent a separation from ordinary augmented-factor-graph dynamic programming.
